evidence: src/infrastructure/persistence/InMemoryOrderRepository.ts: save(order) does `this.records.set(order.id, structuredClone(order.toSnapshot()))`, a deep-copied snapshot.
src/infrastructure/persistence/InMemoryProductRepository.ts: save(product) does `this.records.set(product.id, product.toSnapshot())`, with no clone.

Both files repeat the doc comment: 'Stores snapshots rather than live entities, so changes only become visible once a use case explicitly saves them.' The isolation rule is stated twice and enforced differently.

Both classes copy the same storage mechanics: `private readonly records = new Map<string, XSnapshot>()`, findById/findAll through X.restore(record), and save through toSnapshot(). Nothing shared enforces the invariant.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The concern is cohesive: both files are in-memory, Map-backed repository adapters that implement domain repository ports. They do not split into unrelated concerns, and neither one bypasses the domain abstractions, since both go through toSnapshot()/restore().

The problem is the module's storage invariant. Both files carry the same doc comment saying records are stored as snapshots, not live entities, so changes only become visible after an explicit save. Each class re-implements that rule on its own, and the two copies have drifted apart. InMemoryOrderRepository.save deep-copies the snapshot with structuredClone(order.toSnapshot()). InMemoryProductRepository.save stores product.toSnapshot() directly, with no copy. If ProductSnapshot holds any nested mutable data, the product store can share references with live entities, which breaks the isolation guarantee its own comment promises.

The rest of the snapshot logic is also copied between the classes: the Map<string, Snapshot> storage, findById/findAll through restore, and save. There is no shared base or helper that would keep the invariant in one place. That is the 'duplicated rule or invariant that should live in one place' failure in the rubric, and the drift between the copies is the evidence. Confidence is moderate because ProductSnapshot's shape isn't shown, so I can't confirm the missing copy actually leaks references.

violations.message: save() stores product.toSnapshot() without the structuredClone that InMemoryOrderRepository uses. The snapshot-isolation invariant both files document is copied into each class and has drifted, so this repository may keep references shared with live entities.

Re-implements the snapshot store (Map of snapshots, restore on read, clone on save) separately from InMemoryProductRepository instead of sharing one abstraction. The isolation rule lives in more than one place and the copies are now inconsistent.
